title: Multiple internal hypotheses (+ R1.37 verifier head, R1.38 selection among hypotheses)
question: Does keeping 4 hypothesis heads with a learned score reduce confident wrong answers (confidence >= 0.8 and wrong) compared with one head? Does an independently trained verifier head predict correctness better than the model's own confidence (R1.37), and does picking the hypothesis the verifier prefers beat the model's own pick (R1.38)?

predictions.R1.35: PASS: >= 20% fewer confident errors at no accuracy loss
predictions.R1.37: V1 recorded as R1.37's result: verifier AUROC >= own-confidence AUROC + 0.03 (PASS) — it is trained on external correctness only
predictions.R1.38: S1 and S2 recorded as R1.38's result: selection among 4 latent hypotheses beats a single trajectory and the model's own pick
predictions.compute: 4 heads and a verifier add < 5% FLOPs; selection costs no extra forward passes

not_claimed: Execution hints, multiple-choice learning and learned verifiers are prior art; the measurement on this benchmark is the contribution.
